concerns.text: FR-001 requires retrieving templates from a 'fixed, curated set' stored in assets/templates/. T009b_map introduces an unverified dependency on an external OSF manifest URL and a 'match by task_id prefix' heuristic. If the manifest lacks these rules or the URL is unreachable, the system aborts, making the requirement contingent on external infrastructure not authorized by the spec. A task must exist to verify the manifest content locally or handle the fallback without aborting the entire experiment.

FR-003 mandates executing 'all autonomous agents from the original study'. T022a_gen and T022b hardcode a specific list of 7 agents (Alpha, Beta, etc.) in docs/agent_list.md. If the original study's published list differs from this hardcoded list, the implementation fails to execute the required scope. A task must exist to dynamically parse the original study's agent list or verify the hardcoded list against the source before execution.

SC-004 requires ≥95% of runs to complete successfully. T026 defines 'success rate' as (Total - Excluded - Failed) / (Total - Excluded). This mathematically allows the system to pass the gate even if the absolute number of successful runs is low (e.g., if 40 runs are 'excluded' due to timeouts, the denominator shrinks). A task must exist to calculate the success rate against the fixed 140-run baseline (Total Runs) to ensure the 95% threshold is met in absolute terms.

The spec's edge case for timeouts requires recording a 'Timeout' status and excluding the score. T038 writes the exclusion to results/audit_ids.csv (reusing the 'conflict' schema). This conflates 'Scaffold Conflict' (logic error) with 'Timeout' (resource limit) in a single audit file, making it ambiguous for downstream analysis (T014c/T024) to distinguish between a valid exclusion due to a constraint violation versus a valid exclusion due to infrastructure limits. A task must exist to tag or separate these exclusion types in the audit log.

FR-005 requires the system to 'perform a normality check and select either a paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test accordingly'. T029's description focuses on the logic of the test selection without explicitly mandating the output of the normality check results (Shapiro-Wilk statistic/p-value) to the report, which is required by SC-002 for full transparency of the statistical method selection. A task must exist to explicitly write these statistics to the final report.

T009b fetches templates from an external OSF URL and saves them to assets/templates/. Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) requires that 'Every file under data/ is checksummed' and 'Raw data is preserved unchanged'. While assets/ is distinct from data/, the task does not explicitly include a checksum step for these fetched templates, risking a violation of the 'Single Source of Truth' principle if the fetched content drifts or is modified without a recorded hash. A task must exist to checksum the fetched templates.
